answer: Physical Provenance Chain. Each identity must present a continuous hardware-rooted log from a ferrous-core magnetometer recording its unique factory magnetization pattern at manufacture. A verifier checks the raw copper-trace timing jitter embedded in the device's clock tree, corroborated by the live signal from the sensor array. Cloning requires reproducing both the magnetization and jitter on new silicon, costing roughly $40k per identity plus a fabrication run.
